content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"DDG-51 is the U.S. Navy's Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer program, funded under the Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy account.","citation":{"fact_id":"06b4b0dd3d59e700"}},{"text":"The Navy describes the DDG 51 as able to operate offensively and defensively, independently or as part of Carrier Strike Groups and Surface Action Groups, in multi-threat environments that include air, surface and subsurface threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"7bc24f8d6771099f"}},{"text":"Beginning in FY2017, DDG 51 Flight III ships added the Air and Missile Defense Radar (SPY-6(V)1) to significantly enhance Integrated Air and Missile Defense capability against current and future threats.","citation":{"fact_id":"7bc24f8d6771099f"}},{"text":"Starting in FY2023, the program is upgrading the MK38 Gun Weapon System to the Mod 4 configuration, replacing the WSN-7 inertial navigation system with the follow-on WSN-12, adding 15 additional berths, and replacing the Bridgemaster Surface Search Radar with the Next-Generation Surface Search Radar.","citation":{"fact_id":"7bc24f8d6771099f"}},{"text":"For FY2026 the Department requests a total of $5,410,773 thousand (about $5.4 billion) and a total quantity of two ships.","citation":{"fact_id":"7bc24f8d6771099f"}},{"text":"That FY2026 request combines $10,773 thousand of discretionary funding (quantity of 0) with $5,400,000 thousand of mandatory funding (quantity of 2), supporting the contract award for two FY2026 ships.","citation":{"fact_id":"3e5027104a7d44bb"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"DDG-51 is a large shipbuilding line: FY2024 actual funding totaled $6,366,431 thousand (about $6.4 billion).","citation":{"fact_id":"06b4b0dd3d59e700"}},{"text":"For FY2025, Congress enacted $8,268,628 thousand (about $8.3 billion) for the program.","citation":{"fact_id":"60bc7e5d65d9a69f"}},{"text":"The FY2026 total request drops to $5,410,773 thousand (about $5.4 billion), lower than the prior year's enacted level.","citation":{"fact_id":"99b987eb326c9857"}},{"text":"Most of the FY2026 request comes as a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $5,400,000 thousand rather than through the regular discretionary budget.","citation":{"fact_id":"5adb4183aed84ed8"}},{"text":"Only $10,773 thousand of the FY2026 request is discretionary funding.","citation":{"fact_id":"bc3d2a6091db4104"}},{"text":"The Navy awarded two Multi-year Procurement contracts covering FY2023-FY2027 for 9 ships with options, with the budget reflecting savings from economic order quantity procurement and the multi-year strategy.","citation":{"fact_id":"7bc24f8d6771099f"}},{"text":"DDG-51 FY2024 actuals came in about $1.9 billion above the original PB2024 request, rising from a $4,483,214 thousand request to $6,366,431 thousand in actuals — a roughly 42% increase.","citation":{"fact_id":"8169f40c26f22ffd"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is run by the Department of the Navy (organization code N).","citation":{"fact_id":"06b4b0dd3d59e700"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
